query: In high-entropy alloys, what governs superconducting behavior and why? Formulate one testable mechanistic hypothesis, identify a controlled comparison against a baseline that could reveal the governing cause, predict the relative observations expected if the hypothesis is correct, define its boundary conditions, state what prior evidence would make it plausible, and specify a result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In equiatomic fcc high‐entropy alloys, the superconducting critical temperature (Tc) is governed by the amplitude of atomic‐lattice distortion induced by atomic size mismatch, which modulates the electron–phonon coupling constant λ; alloys with larger size mismatch exhibit enhanced λ and thus higher Tc.
generation.material_initial_state: Single‐phase equiatomic fcc high‐entropy alloy with low to moderate atomic size variance (e.g. CoCrFeNi baseline).
generation.intervention: Substitute one element in the equiatomic alloy (e.g. Ni) with elements of systematically varying atomic radius (e.g. Al, Ti, Cu, Zn) while keeping overall equiatomic composition and crystal structure constant.
generation.conditions: Measurements performed at ambient pressure, temperatures from 0.3 K to 20 K, no intentional magnetic impurities, verified single‐phase fcc by XRD.
generation.structural_mediator: Atomic lattice distortion amplitude (quantified by XRD peak broadening and Debye–Waller factors).
generation.mechanism: Increased lattice distortion broadens the phonon density of states toward lower frequencies, raising the electron–phonon coupling constant λ via enhanced phonon scattering, leading to higher Tc within the BCS framework.
generation.predicted_outcome: As atomic size mismatch increases, lattice distortion amplitude and λ both increase, yielding a systematic rise in Tc of order 0.5–1 K above the baseline (e.g. from ~1.5 K up to ~2.5 K).
generation.baseline: Equiatomic CoCrFeNi (atomic size variance σ ≈ 0.03 Å) exhibiting Tc ≈ 1.5 K and measured λ ≈ 0.6.
generation.boundary: Applies to equiatomic fcc HEAs without magnetic order, within 0–10% substitution range of a single element, Tc below 10 K and ambient pressure; does not apply if phase separation or magnetism emerges.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate: the quantitative relation between mismatch and Tc (slope) may vary by ±50% due to phonon spectrum complexity and disorder effects.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a series of equiatomic fcc HEAs by substituting Ni with Al, Ti, Cu, Zn in 10% increments (keeping four other elements constant). For each alloy: (1) measure lattice distortion via XRD (peak widths, Debye–Waller factors), (2) determine phonon DOS via inelastic neutron scattering, (3) extract λ from tunneling spectroscopy or McMillan‐Allen–Dynes fits, (4) measure Tc via resistivity and susceptibility.
measurements: Phonon density of states (inelastic neutron scattering)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Hypothesis is falsified if across the substitution series there is no statistically significant positive correlation between lattice distortion (or λ) and Tc (e.g., Pearson |R| < 0.3 with p > 0.05).
